            • Global Constraints
            • File Structure
              • Task 1: Economics aggregation — fees, profit factor, expectancy, avg win/loss
              • Task 2: Per-trade holding-in-bars in the economics layer
              • Task 3: Surface entry precision and entry recall in the model layer
              • Task 4: Test infrastructure for the scripts.experiments package
              • Task 5: Typed models for the campaign regime payload
              • Task 6: Builders — parse layer rows and select winners (Level 1)
              • Task 7: Builders — top-N leaderboard (Level 2) and thin-sample marker
              • Task 8: Payload serialization to JSON-safe dicts
              • Task 9: Orchestrate the three lenses per (symbol, labeling config) group
              • Task 10: Render all seven views and three levels from the typed payload
              • Task 11: Wire the payload and marker into report_campaign.py

    • Global Constraints
    • File Structure
      • Task 1: Economics aggregation — fees, profit factor, expectancy, avg win/loss
      • Task 2: Per-trade holding-in-bars in the economics layer
      • Task 3: Surface entry precision and entry recall in the model layer
      • Task 4: Test infrastructure for the scripts.experiments package
      • Task 5: Typed models for the campaign regime payload
      • Task 6: Builders — parse layer rows and select winners (Level 1)
      • Task 7: Builders — top-N leaderboard (Level 2) and thin-sample marker
      • Task 8: Payload serialization to JSON-safe dicts
      • Task 9: Orchestrate the three lenses per (symbol, labeling config) group
      • Task 10: Render all seven views and three levels from the typed payload
      • Task 11: Wire the payload and marker into report_campaign.py
    • Self-Review
    1. Home

    ARCHIVED 2026-07-11 — DONE. All tasks implemented and gate-green.

    Campaign Report Regime Redesign (Part A) Implementation Plan

    For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

    Goal: Turn the campaign report's regime section into a per-regime "which strategy is best" answer — three lenses (economics, scores, labels), all seven taxonomy views, a winner table, a top-N leaderboard and a labels-context block — grouped by (symbol, labeling config), driven off typed models.

    Architecture: The heavy lifting stays where it already lives. The three standalone layer scripts (scripts/analysis/regime/layers/{economics,labels,model}.py) still touch the DB and parquets through the shared helpers and emit JSON; the new economics/score columns are added to the shared polars aggregations they call (rainbow.data_processing.helpers.regime, rainbow.model_trainer.helpers.regime_model_quality), which already have unit tests. A new pure module beside the campaign renderer (scripts/experiments/common/campaign_regime_tables.py + campaign_regime_types.py) turns the per-strategy layer JSON into typed level-1/level-2/level-3 tables; regime_reporting.py orchestrates the layers and renders the typed models to Markdown; report_campaign.py embeds the same typed payload in campaign_report.json. No inline DB or parquet reads are added anywhere.

    Tech Stack: Python 3.11, Polars, frozen slotted dataclasses, pytest, the rainbow.* editable packages.

    Global Constraints

    • Every touched Python file must pass, with no suppressions (# type: ignore / # noqa / pylint: disable are forbidden — fix the root cause):

    • ruff check <file>

    • MYPYPATH="$(ls -d modules/*/src | tr '\n' ':')" .venv/bin/mypy --strict <file>
    • .venv/bin/pyright <file>
    • .venv/bin/pylint <file> — score ≥ 9.5
    • Line length ≤ 120; 4-space indent; UTF-8; PEP8; English everywhere.

    • Type hints on every signature; complete docstrings; comments explain the non-obvious why, never the change history; no plan/task/phase references in code, comments, docstrings, docs or commit messages.

    • Typed objects flow between functions; a model becomes a dict only at the persistence boundary (the JSON write).

    • Formatting always reuses the existing fmt_* family from rainbow.core.helpers.reports — never an inline format. Available: fmt_money, fmt_pct(value, *, already_pct=False, signed=False), fmt_decimal(value, digits=3), fmt_count, fmt_f1, fmt_js, fmt_sharpe, fmt_money_with_return, fmt_trades_entry, fmt_seconds, fmt_minutes, fmt_int, fmt_signed_float. There is no fmt_ratio or fmt_bars; use fmt_decimal for ratios/bar counts.

    • New display-name columns require a legend entry in the report's legend source before any regeneration is published; a fallback legend blocks publication.

    • Sample size never filters or reorders and never penalizes: zero trades is a valid abstention. The informative marker is display-only; its default threshold is 0.02 (2% of a bucket's ticks), a report parameter.

    • Never regenerate straight onto a canonical report path and never byte-copy staging onto canonical; the operational regeneration follows stage → verify → publish (a human workflow, out of code scope here).

    • Do not commit or run long processes without explicit instruction.

    • [x] Step 3: Implement the new aggregations

    Replace the body of aggregate_economics_by_regime (regime.py:556-590) — keep the docstring, extend it — with:

    def aggregate_economics_by_regime(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    regime_column: str,
    net_pnl_column: str = "pnl",
    gross_pnl_column: str = "gross_pnl",
    holding_bars_column: str = "holding_bars",
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate per-regime economics from a closed-trade frame.

    Emits, per bucket: trade count and share, win rate, total and per-trade net and gross PnL, fees
    (summed gross minus summed net), expectancy (mean net PnL), profit factor (summed positive net over the
    absolute summed negative net; ``None`` when the bucket has no losing trade), and average winning and
    losing net PnL. When ``holding_bars_column`` is present in ``frame`` the mean holding in bars is added.

    Args:
        frame: One row per closed trade, carrying ``regime_column``, ``net_pnl_column``,
            ``gross_pnl_column`` and optionally ``holding_bars_column``.
        regime_column: Name of the taxonomy/regime column to group by.
        net_pnl_column: Net-PnL column name.
        gross_pnl_column: Gross-PnL column name.
        holding_bars_column: Optional per-trade holding-in-bars column; averaged only when present.

    Returns:
        One row per regime bucket, sorted by descending trade count.
    """
    total_trades = frame.height
    has_holding = holding_bars_column in frame.columns
    aggregations: list[pl.Expr] = [
        pl.len().alias("trades_count"),
        (pl.col(net_pnl_column) > 0.0).mean().alias("win_rate"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).sum().alias("total_pnl"),
        pl.col(gross_pnl_column).sum().alias("total_gross_pnl"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).mean().alias("net_per_trade"),
        pl.col(gross_pnl_column).mean().alias("gross_per_trade"),
        (pl.col(gross_pnl_column).sum() - pl.col(net_pnl_column).sum()).alias("fees"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).mean().alias("expectancy"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).filter(pl.col(net_pnl_column) > 0.0).sum().alias("_gross_profit"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).filter(pl.col(net_pnl_column) < 0.0).sum().alias("_gross_loss"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).filter(pl.col(net_pnl_column) > 0.0).mean().alias("avg_win"),
        pl.col(net_pnl_column).filter(pl.col(net_pnl_column) < 0.0).mean().alias("avg_loss"),
    ]
    if has_holding:
        aggregations.append(pl.col(holding_bars_column).mean().alias("avg_holding_bars"))
    return (
        frame.group_by(regime_column)
        .agg(aggregations)
        .with_columns((pl.col("trades_count") / float(total_trades)).alias("share"))
        .with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col("_gross_loss").abs() > 0.0)
            .then(pl.col("_gross_profit") / pl.col("_gross_loss").abs())
            .otherwise(None)
            .alias("profit_factor")
        )
        .drop("_gross_profit", "_gross_loss")
        .sort("trades_count", descending=True)
    )

    • [x] Step 4: Implement the layer change

    In scripts/analysis/regime/layers/economics.py, replace _closed_trades_frame with:

    def _closed_trades_frame(closed_trades: list[Any], *, bar_seconds: float | None) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Build the ``(opened_at, closed_at, pnl, gross_pnl[, holding_bars])`` frame the aggregation joins on.

    When ``bar_seconds`` is given, a ``holding_bars`` column is added — the realized trade duration expressed
    in base-timeframe bars, so per-regime average holding is reported in bars rather than wall-clock time.
    When it is ``None`` the column is omitted and the downstream aggregation reports no average holding.
    """
    frame = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "opened_at": [trade.opened_at for trade in closed_trades],
            "closed_at": [trade.closed_at for trade in closed_trades],
            "pnl": [trade.net_pnl for trade in closed_trades],
            "gross_pnl": [trade.gross_pnl for trade in closed_trades],
        }
    )
    if bar_seconds is None:
        return frame
    return frame.with_columns(
        ((pl.col("closed_at") - pl.col("opened_at")).dt.total_seconds() / float(bar_seconds)).alias(
            "holding_bars"
        )
    )

Ensure the regime attach join still uses event_time_column="opened_at" (the new columns ride along untouched).

    def _entry_binary_stats(y_true: list[int], y_pred: list[int]) -> BinaryStats:
    """Trade-vs-no-trade binary stats for a bucket (a class id other than NONE means 'trade')."""
    true_positive = false_positive = false_negative = true_negative = 0
    for true_id, pred_id in zip(y_true, y_pred, strict=True):
        true_is_trade = true_id != NONE_LABEL_ID
        pred_is_trade = pred_id != NONE_LABEL_ID
        if pred_is_trade and true_is_trade:
            true_positive += 1
        elif pred_is_trade and not true_is_trade:
            false_positive += 1
        elif not pred_is_trade and true_is_trade:
            false_negative += 1
        else:
            true_negative += 1
    return build_binary_stats(tp=true_positive, fp=false_positive, fn=false_negative, tn=true_negative)

    Create scripts/experiments/common/campaign_regime_types.py:

    """Typed models for the campaign report's regime section.

These frozen dataclasses are the single in-memory representation of the campaign regime analysis. The
Markdown renderer and the ``campaign_report.json`` serializer both read them, so the two outputs cannot
drift. Every optional field means the same thing everywhere: ``None`` is "not applicable / not defined for
this bucket" (for example, no economics row when a strategy took no trades in a regime), never zero.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)


class EconomicsBucketRow:
    """One strategy's per-regime economics for a single taxonomy bucket."""

    regime: str
    trades_count: int
    share: float
    exposure_share: float
    win_rate: float
    total_pnl: float
    total_gross_pnl: float
    net_per_trade: float
    gross_per_trade: float
    fees: float
    expectancy: float
    avg_win: float | None
    avg_loss: float | None
    profit_factor: float | None
    avg_holding_bars: float | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)


class ScoresBucketRow:
    """One strategy's per-regime signal quality (prediction-vs-label) for a single taxonomy bucket."""

    regime: str
    bars: int
    share: float
    entry_count: int
    accuracy: float
    entry_precision: float
    entry_recall: float
    entry_f1: float
    macro_f1: float
    js_divergence: float

    """Pure builders that turn per-strategy regime layer JSON into the typed campaign regime models.

No database or parquet access happens here: the layer scripts produce the JSON, and these functions only
reshape already-parsed dictionaries into the typed models the renderer and JSON serializer consume.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from typing import Any

from scripts.experiments.common.campaign_regime_types import (
    EconomicsBucketRow,
    LabelsBucketRow,
    ScoresBucketRow,
    StrategyBucketMetrics,
    WinnerRow,
)


def _opt_float(value: Any) -> float | None:
    """Coerce a JSON scalar to an optional float (``None`` stays ``None``)."""
    return None if value is None else float(value)


def economics_row_from_dict(raw: Mapping[str, Any], *, exposure_share: float) -> EconomicsBucketRow:
    """Build an economics bucket row from one layer JSON bucket dict."""
    return EconomicsBucketRow(
        regime=str(raw["regime"]),
        trades_count=int(raw["trades_count"]),
        share=float(raw["share"]),
        exposure_share=exposure_share,
        win_rate=float(raw["win_rate"]),
        total_pnl=float(raw["total_pnl"]),
        total_gross_pnl=float(raw["total_gross_pnl"]),
        net_per_trade=float(raw["net_per_trade"]),
        gross_per_trade=float(raw["gross_per_trade"]),
        fees=float(raw["fees"]),
        expectancy=float(raw["expectancy"]),
        avg_win=_opt_float(raw.get("avg_win")),
        avg_loss=_opt_float(raw.get("avg_loss")),
        profit_factor=_opt_float(raw.get("profit_factor")),
        avg_holding_bars=_opt_float(raw.get("avg_holding_bars")),
    )


def scores_row_from_dict(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ScoresBucketRow:
    """Build a scores bucket row from one layer JSON bucket dict."""
    return ScoresBucketRow(
        regime=str(raw["regime"]),
        bars=int(raw["count"]),
        share=float(raw["share"]),
        entry_count=int(raw["entry_count"]),
        accuracy=float(raw["accuracy"]),
        entry_precision=float(raw["entry_precision"]),
        entry_recall=float(raw["entry_recall"]),
        entry_f1=float(raw["entry_f1"]),
        macro_f1=float(raw["macro_f1"]),
        js_divergence=float(raw["js_divergence"]),
    )


def labels_row_from_dict(raw: Mapping[str, Any], *, exposure_share: float) -> LabelsBucketRow:
    """Build a labels bucket row from one layer JSON bucket dict."""
    return LabelsBucketRow(
        regime=str(raw["regime"]),
        bars=int(raw["count"]),
        exposure_share=exposure_share,
        long_share=float(raw["long_share"]),
        short_share=float(raw["short_share"]),
        none_share=float(raw["none_share"]),
        strength=float(raw["label_strength_avg"]),
        quality=float(raw["label_quality_avg"]),
    )


def build_winner_rows(
    strategy_metrics_by_bucket: Mapping[str, Sequence[StrategyBucketMetrics]],
    *,
    ticks_by_bucket: Mapping[str, int],
    bucket_order: Sequence[str],
) -> tuple[WinnerRow, ...]:
    """Select, per bucket, the best strategy by total net PnL and the best by entry F1.

    Economics winner is chosen only among strategies that took at least one trade in the bucket (an
    abstaining strategy has no economics row and cannot win the money lens). The scores winner is chosen
    among all strategies that have a scores row, so correct abstention can still win the signal lens. Ties
    are broken by strategy name for determinism.
    """
    winners: list[WinnerRow] = []
    for bucket in bucket_order:
        metrics = strategy_metrics_by_bucket.get(bucket, ())
        if not metrics:
            continue
        economics_candidates = [m for m in metrics if m.economics is not None]
        scores_candidates = [m for m in metrics if m.scores is not None]
        best_economics = min(
            economics_candidates,
            key=lambda m: (-(m.economics.total_pnl if m.economics else 0.0), m.strategy),
            default=None,
        )
        best_scores = min(
            scores_candidates,
            key=lambda m: (-(m.scores.entry_f1 if m.scores else 0.0), m.strategy),
            default=None,
        )
        trades = sum(m.economics.trades_count for m in economics_candidates)
        winners.append(
            WinnerRow(
                regime=bucket,
                ticks=int(ticks_by_bucket.get(bucket, 0)),
                trades=trades,
                best_economics_strategy=best_economics.strategy if best_economics else None,
                best_economics_net_pnl=(
                    best_economics.economics.total_pnl
                    if best_economics and best_economics.economics
                    else None
                ),
                best_scores_strategy=best_scores.strategy if best_scores else None,
                best_scores_entry_f1=(
                    best_scores.scores.entry_f1 if best_scores and best_scores.scores else None
                ),
            )
        )
    return tuple(winners)

    _TOP_N_27 = 3
_TOP_N_9_OR_3 = 5


def view_top_n(taxonomy: str) -> int:
    """Row cap for a taxonomy view: 3 for the 27-state view, 5 for every 9-state and 3-state view."""
    return _TOP_N_27 if taxonomy == "taxonomy_27_full" else _TOP_N_9_OR_3


def is_thin(economics: EconomicsBucketRow | None, *, ticks: int, marker_threshold: float) -> bool:
    """Report whether a ranking rests on thin activity (traded on < threshold share of the bucket ticks).

    Abstention (no economics row) is never thin: staying out of a regime is a valid decision, not thin
    evidence.
    """
    if economics is None or ticks <= 0:
        return False
    return economics.trades_count < marker_threshold * float(ticks)


def build_bucket_leaderboard(
    metrics: Sequence[StrategyBucketMetrics],
    *,
    taxonomy: str,
    ticks: int,
    marker_threshold: float,
) -> BucketLeaderboard:
    """Rank a bucket's strategies by descending total net PnL and keep the view's top-N.

    Strategies with no economics row (pure abstention) sort after those that traded; ties break by strategy
    name. The full economics and scores metrics ride along on every row so a JSON consumer can re-rank by
    the scores lens without recomputation.
    """
    regime = metrics[0].economics.regime if metrics and metrics[0].economics else (
        metrics[0].scores.regime if metrics and metrics[0].scores else ""
    )
    ordered = sorted(
        metrics,
        key=lambda m: (
            0 if m.economics is not None else 1,
            -(m.economics.total_pnl if m.economics else 0.0),
            m.strategy,
        ),
    )
    rows = tuple(
        LeaderboardRow(
            rank=index + 1,
            strategy=item.strategy,
            economics=item.economics,
            scores=item.scores,
            thin=is_thin(item.economics, ticks=ticks, marker_threshold=marker_threshold),
        )
        for index, item in enumerate(ordered[: view_top_n(taxonomy)])
    )
    return BucketLeaderboard(regime=regime, rows=rows)

def _scores_to_dict(row: ScoresBucketRow | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Serialize a scores row (or ``None``)."""
    return None if row is None else asdict(row)


def campaign_regime_payload_to_dict(payload: CampaignRegimePayload) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Serialize the typed campaign regime payload into JSON-safe primitives.

    Datetimes are written as ISO-8601 UTC strings; every section, taxonomy view and level is preserved so
    ``campaign_report.json`` carries the same information the Markdown renders (and both ranking orders are
    derivable from the leaderboard rows, which keep the full economics and scores metrics).
    """
    return {
        "marker_threshold": payload.marker_threshold,
        "sections": [
            {
                "symbol": section.symbol,
                "labeling_config_hash": section.labeling_config_hash,
                "ranges": [
                    [isoformat_utc(start), isoformat_utc(end)] for start, end in section.ranges
                ],
                "views": [
                    {
                        "taxonomy": view.taxonomy,
                        "winners": [asdict(winner) for winner in view.winners],
                        "leaderboards": [
                            {
                                "regime": board.regime,
                                "rows": [
                                    {
                                        "rank": row.rank,
                                        "strategy": row.strategy,
                                        "thin": row.thin,
                                        "economics": _economics_to_dict(row.economics),
                                        "scores": _scores_to_dict(row.scores),
                                    }
                                    for row in board.rows
                                ],
                            }
                            for board in view.leaderboards
                        ],
                        "labels": [asdict(label) for label in view.labels],
                    }
                    for view in section.views
                ],
            }
            for section in payload.sections
        ],
    }
